title: How Kids Learn to Make Friends
hook: Sharing and taking turns aren't automatic — they develop gradually through play. Preschoolers grow real social skills with practice, and adults coach by modeling and naming.
key_points: Sharing, turn-taking, and cooperation develop gradually; preschoolers slowly compete less and cooperate more.
Play with peers is where social, emotional, and language skills actually grow.
Around age 3, kids can start working out disputes by taking turns or trading — but they need adult encouragement.
Adults coach by modeling calm problem-solving, naming feelings, and offering supervised playdates.
content_html: Friendship skills look effortless in adults, but for young children they're learned, not built-in. The AAP describes preschool social development as gradual: as children move through ages three to five, they slowly compete less and cooperate more, becoming more aware of other people's feelings. Sharing and taking turns are part of this slow climb, not switches that flip on at a certain birthday.
extra_html: Play with peers is the real classroom — it's where social, emotional, and language skills grow, and where children discover that not everyone thinks the way they do. Around age three, kids can begin working out disputes by taking turns or trading toys, though they still need adults to encourage it. Caregivers coach best by modeling calm problem-solving, helping children name their feelings, encouraging "use your words" instead of acting out, and setting up supervised playdates for practice. This is general guidance; if you're concerned about your child's social development, talk to your pediatrician.

related.title: Play Is How Young Children Learn
related.hook: For young children, play isn't a break from learning — it is the learning, building language, problem-solving, and social skills all at once.

related.title: What School Readiness Really Means
related.hook: Being ready for school is less about reading early and more about social and emotional skills — following directions, taking turns, and managing feelings.

choices.text: Gradually, through play and with adult encouragement
All at once, the moment a child turns three
Only if a child is naturally generous from birth

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP describes these as skills that grow gradually. Around age 3 children begin trading and taking turns, but they still need adult coaching.

flashcards.prompt: What are two ways adults can coach preschoolers' social skills?
flashcards.back_html: Model calm problem-solving and conflict resolution by example, and name feelings to reduce frustration — supervised playdates give kids room to practice.
